{{nihongo|'''Kasumekentou Shrine'''|糟目犬頭神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Miyaji-chō, Okazaki|Q107420129|qid=Q107420129|lt=Miyaji-chō}}, {{ill|Okazaki, Aichi|Q242783|qid=Q242783}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is selected as one of the {{ill|100 Brilliant Okazaki Tourist Sites|Q11472991|qid=Q11472991}}<ref>[http://www.city.okazaki.aichi.jp/350/351/p006883_d/fil/1.pdf List of 100 Brilliant Okazaki Tourist Sites]</ref>. {{nihongo|'''Kasumekentou Shrine'''|糟目犬頭神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mikawa Province]].

== Overview ==
It is regarded as one of the six shikinaisha in {{ill|Hekikai District|Q5368803|qid=Q5368803}} listed in volumes 9-10 of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. In {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} 1 ({{ill|701|Q23496|qid=Q23496}}), it was built enshrining {{ill|Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto}}. It was formerly in Nishikasume Morisaki of neighboring Kamiwada village and was therefore called Kasume Shrine, but repeated flooding moved it to the current location.

In {{ill|Eien|Q1324864|qid=Q1324864}} 1 ({{ill|987|Q23644|qid=Q23644}}), Kumano Sansho Daigongen was jointly enshrined. It is said that in {{ill|Kannō|Q1145053|qid=Q1145053}} 1 ({{ill|1350|Q6094|qid=Q6094}}), {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}} donated 100 kanmon as land for Kumano Gongen.

The Okazaki domain lord {{ill|Honda Yasushige (daimyo, born 1554)|Q10522159|qid=Q10522159}} protected this shrine and rebuilt the honden in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 7 ({{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}}). In Keichō 10 ({{ill|1605|Q6741|qid=Q6741}}), he dedicated a torii made of {{ill|Shakudani Stone|Q11599510|qid=Q11599510}} from Echizen<ref>[http://www.city.okazaki.lg.jp/100th/topics/p020876_d/fil/41mutsumiseibu.pdf Mutsumi West School District | Okazaki Town Stories District Page | Okazaki City 100th Anniversary Site]</ref>.

A red-seal grant from {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}}, dated August 28, Keichō 8 ({{ill|1603|Q6735|qid=Q6735}}), bestowed 43 koku of shrine lands. The same document says "Inugashira Shrine lands," and a red-seal grant of {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|Q314464|qid=Q314464}} in {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} 3 ({{ill|1617|Q6798|qid=Q6798}}) also says "Inugashira lands," showing that in the early modern period it was publicly called Inugashira Shrine.

This shrine is the starting point of the Tsutsumidōri Teyaga Otaōgi Festival<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date= |url=http://webhp.city.okazaki.lg.jp/appli/07/2shou6.pdf |title=Okazaki City Historical Landscape Maintenance and Improvement Plan - Chapter 2 Historical landscape seen in rice-cultivation rites of the Mutsumi district |format=PDF |publisher={{ill|Okazaki City Hall|ja|岡崎市役所|qid=Q11472848}} |accessdate=2018-4-1 }}</ref>. Children's sumo is held at the autumn grand festival.
